interpretation: The prior 13.287713 process-CPU/wall anomaly was not reproduced in this single controlled hosted Linux run. All 80 ratios were at or below 4.008956678 on a four-CPU affinity set, and per-thread CPU sums closely tracked process CPU time. This does not identify the cause of the older anomaly and is not physical-hardware replication.
limitations: One GitHub-hosted x86-64 virtual runner only; not an independent physical-hardware replication.
The arithmetic loop is synthetic and does not measure DRAM bandwidth or a representative scientific application.
The cgroup cpu.stat counters are cgroup-wide and may include other processes; they are not attributed to this benchmark process.
The cgroup metadata is read at the process cgroup; cgroup v2 threaded subtrees can distribute threads across sub-cgroups, and this run does not record per-thread cgroup membership.
Only the current cgroup cpu.max value is recorded; ancestor bandwidth quotas are not enumerated.
No perf_event task-clock, hardware performance counters, RSS or native-allocation measurements were collected.
The 0.25 CPU anomaly margin is a diagnostic threshold, not a statistical confidence bound.
